contract.words: Collect $3,000 of settled cash within 45 days. I can invest up to $3,000, but I can give it at most 1 hour a week of my own time — Brain and any contractors have to do the rest.

strategy.title: Resell one-time Google Business Profile optimization at $300 to US local service businesses by cold email, fulfilled by a Fiverr GBP seller
strategy.why: Smallest cash at risk per test and buyer-funded fulfilment: each order's $50 Fiverr cost is incurred only after the buyer's $300 is paid, so the only pre-proof spend is $47 of sending tooling. Eleven orders settle $3,201 net of Stripe fees inside 45 days if they close by day 30; owner time is 3.2 of the 6 hours allowed. Whether cold buyers pay $300 and at what close rate is unknown and is measured by the first 14 days of sending.

alternatives.title: Website rebuild subcontracted to a Fiverr developer at $1,200
alternatives.why: Only three sales needed, but $600 deposits tied up per job, a 21-day time to cash and longer delivery leave less room to measure and still settle in 45 days; price and close rate equally unestablished.

alternatives.title: Upwork fixed-price content jobs with a subcontracted writer
alternatives.why: Upwork holds fixed-price funds up to 14 days in review plus a 5-day security hold, so cash lands 25 days after work starts; a new profile's win rate is unknown and the $120 writer cost cuts margin.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right stance (price, close rate and the Fiverr fulfiller are all RECOMMENDATION-only; a live test is the only way to measure them; the verified research found no buyer-paid price), and the arithmetic mostly holds: 11 x $300 = $3,300 gross, Stripe 2.9% + $0.30 = $9.00 x 11 = $99, settled $3,201 >= $3,000; costs $550 Fiverr + $94 Instantly + $99 fees = $743 <= $3,000 cap; owner hours 1 + 11 x 0.2 = 3.2 h of ~6.4 h (1 h/week x 45 days), with week 1 at exactly 1 h. But the validation contradicts the contract's proof condition: the contract says 'First paid order settled in the owner's account before scaling spend', while the plan's proof is '2 orders paid through the Stripe link by day 14', and its own ledger settles the first receipts on day 24 (card timeToFirstCash: first Stripe payout 7-14 days after the first live payment). The plan keeps sending and orders 3 more Fiverr jobs on day 18, i.e. scales spend before anything has settled. The strategy also claims the only pre-proof spend is $47; Brain's trace shows $165 pre-proof and $342 peak exposure because Fiverr is paid on day 10 while the buyer's money only lands on day 24, so fulfilment is not buyer-funded in cash terms.
findings: Proof must be the first payout settled in the owner's bank (about day 17-24), not a Stripe payment; the continue rule and the day-18 batch must wait for it, or the plan must state that the scaling is within a ceiling the owner approved before proof.
Recompute the schedule with the gate moved: first settlement ~day 24 leaves ~21 days; check that 11 orders (or fewer, if the remaining ones settle on Stripe's rolling payout) still settle by day 45.
Correct the 'only $47 pre-proof' and 'buyer-funded fulfilment' statements: pre-proof outlay is $165 (Instantly $47 + Fiverr $100 + fees $18) and peak exposure $342.

State the sending volume needed: proof at >=2 orders per 1,000 emails implies ~5,500 emails for 11 orders by day 30; Instantly Growth's sending capacity and a list of that size are not on the card (buyerVolume for this opening is still an open, parked question).
The stop rule 'fewer than 5 paid orders by day 24' should be derived from the moved settlement date, not asserted.
